constraints: In 4D local mode or remote mode, the time parameter is ignored/cannot be used; it is only honored when QUIT 4D is called on 4D Server (in a stored procedure).

With 4D local/remote mode: if an On Exit database method exists, 4D runs it in a newly created local process before quitting (it can delay but not cancel the quit); if no On Exit method exists, 4D aborts every running process immediately, discarding any unsaved data entry.

With 4D Server: QUIT 4D is asynchronous (the calling method is not interrupted), time sets a timeout in seconds before the server actually quits (waits for all clients to disconnect if omitted), and it triggers a client-side dialog plus, after the delay, the On Server Shutdown database method.
